text:
incident-bot: PAGED: infer-pool-east - multiple nodes NotReady (kubelet restart surge) :rotating_light:

incident-bot: Symptoms: node flapping, container restarts, increased 5xxs for realtime-completions, automated routing failing on some requests

sophie: oncall here, ack. grabbing metrics and nodes list

mike: seeing a cluster of NotReady in eu-east-1a and us-east-1b, roughly 6 nodes flapping in last 5m. spike in pod evictions too

raj: logs show repeated kubelet crashes, journalctl has "kubelet: runtime error: out of memory" on several hosts. suspect kubelet OOM+OOM-killer near time of driver resets

elaine: GPU driver resets around same time — nvidia-smi shows GPU reset counters incrementing on the affected hosts

mike: kubectl snippet I ran:
```
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide | egrep "NotReady|SchedulingDisabled"
node-az1-037 NotReady  
node-az1-039 NotReady  
node-az2-101 Ready  
```

raj: Also saw a handful of inference pods CrashLoopBackOff with logs including "CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION" and "failed to allocate memory for model KV cache"

sophie: customer impact? which routes are failing / are we autoscaling around this?

mike: Increased 5xx rate on route /v1/completions-realtime (~12% -> 28%), 95th latency up 3x. Top customers by errors: acme-chat, notable-inc. They're seeing dropped requests and long tail latencies

infra-bot: Auto-scaler attempted to launch warm standby nodes but several launch attempts failed due to boot-time driver crash; rolling retries in progress

raj: mitigation plan: 1) cordon/fluent drain the repeatedly flapping nodes 2) scale up warm-fallback pool (cpu-backed and smaller quantized model) 3) temporarily route high-priority customers to dedicated capacity if available 4) enable aggressive prefix KV cache to reduce token pressure

elaine: I'll cordon node-az1-037 and node-az1-039 now, then evict pods gracefully.

sophie: please paste commands you run. ops, prepare rollback routing if drains cause more pressure

elaine:
```
kubectl cordon node-az1-037
kubectl drain node-az1-037 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
```

mike: starting a scale-up: bumping warm-pool by +4 GPUs and adding 4 cpu-fallback replicas for completions-route

ops: routing change ready: will switch 20% of traffic to cpu-fallback model group to relieve GPU pressure. will roll to 50% if 5xxs don't improve

sophie: good. raj, are we sure kubelet OOM is root cause vs driver bug?"journalctl -u kubelet" grep output?

raj: paste from node-az1-037:
```
Mar 17 12:34:08 kubelet[1234]: runtime: out of memory
Mar 17 12:34:09 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4321 (containerd-shim) score 987
Mar 17 12:34:09 kubelet[1234]: E03017 12:34:09 kubelet_node.go:123] kubelet runtime service crashed: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to start container: Error response from daemon: driver returned unexpected error: cuda: device-side assert triggered
```

mike: that looks like a mix — host-level memory pressure plus GPU driver assert. Could be a recent kernel+driver combo. We rolled a driver update to a subset of hosts in last week (canary) — check node annotation rollout

infra-bot: nodes with annotation driver-version=510.73 were targeted in canary; 6 of the affected nodes match that annotation

elaine: actioned cordon/drain on two nodes, evictions progressing. starting node reboot on node-az1-037 to clear driver state

sophie: ops, execute routing change now and monitor errors + latency. mike, continue scale-up. raj, keep digging on kernel/driver roll. I'll notify SRE lead and apprise support about affected customers

ops: routing change applied -> 20% to cpu-fallback group. monitoring

mike: warm pool scale-up initiated: +4 GPU nodes requested; 2 launched ok, 2 failing with driver init error, teams continuing retries

raj: quick mitigation idea: disable recent driver canary label to prevent new scheduling onto suspect hosts and kick off rolling driver rollback (or pin to previous driver)

infra-bot: removing driver-version=510.73 from scheduler for infer pools (annotation set)

elaine: reboots completed on two nodes, they came back Ready after kubelet restart and rejoin. observing improved pod placements on healthy nodes

sophie: what's the 5xx now?

mike: 5xxs dropped from 28% -> 9% after routing change + drains. latency back down to 1.4x baseline. still higher than normal but improving

raj: root cause hypothesis: interaction between driver 510.73 and recent kernel patch causing memory accounting regression leading to kubelet hitting OOM under high-memory KV-cache workloads; driver assert causes container-level GPU errors

elaine: immediate mitigations: rollback driver canary, cordon affected hosts, increase cpu-fallback routing, scale-up healthy warm pool. longer-term: add node-level oomguard and kernel-driver sanity checks in deployment pipeline

sophie: agree. I've created INC-2026-0048 with summary + action items: postmortem, driver rollback plan, add oomguard, customer outreach for acme-chat & notable-inc. tagging eng-runtime and infra teams

ops: routing back to 40% cpu-fallback while warm pool stabilizes; will revert to normal once 5xx < 1% for 10m

mike: will follow up in postmortem with pod-level mem requests/limits tuning and KV cache caps to avoid host pressure

sophie: thanks all. keep this thread updated with when driver rollback completed and when warm pool fully healthy. if any customer escalations come in, ping me directly @sophie

infra-bot: Driver rollback job queued for canary hosts; will execute in 10m window and report status here

last: labelling for handoff: next oncall (elaine) taking primary follow-ups for recovery runbook and postmortem notes

elaine: ack, taking handoff. will file full timeline and collect logs into the incident doc

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations in place, partial recovery. investigation ongoing.
